data.title: Warts (verruca) — viva
data.summary: Viral infections · 8 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Warts (verruca)** (Viral infections)_

**Q1. What are warts and what causes them?**
- Benign epidermal proliferations caused by human papillomavirus (HPV — DNA virus, >200 types) infecting basal keratinocytes through microabrasions

**Q2. Clinical types and HPV types?**
- Verruca vulgaris (HPV 2, 4, 27, 57), plantar/myrmecia (HPV 1), plane/flat warts (HPV 3, 10), filiform/digitate (face), periungual, mosaic warts, butcher's warts (HPV 7)
- Anogenital: HPV 6, 11 (low risk); 16, 18 (high risk)
- Epidermodysplasia verruciformis: HPV 5, 8

**Q3. Why is it a wart and not a corn?**
- Paring a wart shows black dots (thrombosed capillaries) and interruption of skin lines; corn has a central translucent core, painful on direct pressure, skin lines preserved; lateral squeeze painful in wart

**Q4. Histopathology?**
- Hyperkeratosis, papillomatosis, acanthosis, parakeratosis over papillae ('church spire'), koilocytes (vacuolated cells with perinuclear halo), large keratohyaline granules, inward-pointing rete ridges

**Q5. Treatment options?**
- Destructive: salicylic acid 15–26% paint, cryotherapy, electrocautery, laser, TCA, cantharidin, curettage
- Antiproliferative: 5-FU, bleomycin intralesional (1 U/mL), podophyllotoxin (genital), retinoids (plane warts)
- Immunotherapy: imiquimod, intralesional MMR/Candida antigen/PPD/Mw vaccine, DPCP/SADBE, cimetidine, zinc, HPV vaccine (off-label)

**Q6. What is Koebner phenomenon in warts?**
- Pseudo-Koebner — linear warts along scratch marks due to autoinoculation (also seen in molluscum)

**Q7. Warts in special situations?**
- Children: many regress spontaneously (2/3 in 2 years) — gentle treatments
- Immunocompromised/transplant: extensive, recalcitrant, risk of SCC
- Pregnancy: cryotherapy/TCA; avoid podophyllin

**Q8. Prevention?**
- HPV vaccine (quadrivalent/9-valent) prevents anogenital warts; avoid sharing footwear, cover warts in pools

## Quick spotter facts
- Rough hyperkeratotic papule with black dots — verruca vulgaris

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Anogenital warts; topical agents — 5-FU, bleomycin); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.20. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
